title: Introduce multi-block SystemPrompt data model and transport path
objective: Upgrade the Go prompt path from a single system string to a multi-block system prompt pipeline compatible with the original implementation, while preserving legacy callers.
context: Go currently builds a single string via prompt.BuildSystemPrompt and passes it as provider.Params.System.
The original TypeScript implementation represents system prompts as ordered string arrays and transforms them into API text blocks later.
This is the foundational task for context injection, cache scopes, and parity golden tests.
deliverables: Add SystemPrompt and SystemPromptBlock types with text plus optional source/name/cache metadata.
Add a prompt builder API that returns blocks without removing the existing BuildSystemPrompt compatibility API.
Thread system prompt blocks through engine, loop, and provider Params.
Make provider implementations consume SystemParts or the new block type while preserving string fallback behavior.
Update or add tests that prove the main query path can send multiple system blocks.
acceptance: Anthropic provider can receive and emit multiple system text blocks.
OpenAI and Responses providers still produce a stable joined system prompt.
Existing prompt, provider, and loop tests pass.
No prompt copy or semantic migration is included in this task beyond transport support.
non_goals: Do not migrate the original prompt prose in this task.
Do not implement cache scope decisions in this task.
Do not change agent-specific built-in prompts except where required for type compatibility.
handoff_notes: Keep legacy string entry points working so downstream tasks can land incrementally.
